lessons.lesson: Today I learned the `prime?` function requires a closing `)` after the `sqrt` calculation to prevent parse errors.
Today I learned (expt base exp) requires the exponent as the second argument, not the first.
Today I learned (prime? 4) incorrectly returned #t because I forgot to check even numbers before the loop.
Today I learned the `while` loop condition requires the bound variable to be strictly less than the target.
Today I learned `prime?` requires a boolean argument, not a list of comparisons.
Today I learned `prime?` must check divisibility by all primes up to sqrt(n), not just the hardcoded list [2, 3, 5, 7, 9].
Today I learned the prime? function incorrectly used the argument order, passing the count instead of the number itself.
Today I learned the `quotient` function requires the denominator as the second argument, not the first.
Today I learned the verify gate rejects answers where the stored result differs from the correct calculation.
Today I learned `truncate` is a built-in function, not a user-defined variable, so `set!` cannot rebind it.
